A cost anomaly was detected in a cloud billing dataset. Your job is root cause analysis: identify the resource(s) responsible for the anomalous cost change.

Anomaly details (from anomaly.json, also in your working directory):
{
    "date": "2025-09-22",
    "account_id": "tVENWJP"
}

The file data.csv in your working directory contains the daily cost data for the accounts. Investigate it with code (inspect the columns first) and determine which resource(s) caused the anomalous cost for this account on this date. A resource is identified by its name (the exact value as it appears in data.csv) and its type (the data.csv column that value comes from, written in title case with spaces instead of underscores, e.g. a value from a column named some_column has type "Some Column").

Recommended method (aim to finish in about 6-8 tool calls):
1. Inspect the columns and filter to the anomalous account. Compare the anomaly date with a baseline of the preceding normal days.
2. For EVERY categorical column (not only one), compute the cost change per value between the baseline and the anomaly date. Do this for all columns in a single tool call.
3. Decide which column is the root-cause dimension: the one whose values explain the total cost change most fully and most specifically. A change in one column often shows up indirectly in other columns, so compare the columns before choosing; do not assume a particular column.
4. The root cause can be one value or many values of that column. Include every value that materially drives the change, and nothing else.
5. Answer.

Required final answer format (JSON inside <answer></answer> tags):
{"resource": [{"name": "<resource name>", "type": "<resource type>"}]}
List every resource that is a root cause; include only root causes.

# num_instances per instance_family
for col in ['instance_family']:
    b=base.groupby(col).num_instances.mean()
    a=anom.groupby(col).num_instances.sum()
    chg=(a-b).sort_values(key=abs,ascending=False)
    print('=== num_instances per',col,'=== total:',chg.sum())
    for v in chg.index[:8]:

# price per instance_family
for col in ['instance_family']:
    b=base.groupby(col).price.mean()
    a=anom.groupby(col).price.mean()
    chg=(a-b).sort_values(key=abs,ascending=False)
    print('=== price per',col,'===')
    for v in chg.index[:8]:
        print(f'  {v}: base={b.get(v,0):.4f} anom={a.get(v,0):.4f} chg={chg[v]:+.4f}')

# check which instance families are new on anomaly day

print('new fams:',a_fams-b_fams,'gone fams:',b_fams-a_fams)
# rows for top changed family on anomaly day

print(base[base.instance_family==fam].groupby('date').unblended_cost.sum().tail(5))

import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
sub = df[df.account_id=='tVENWJP'].copy()
anomaly='9/22/2025'
base_dates=[f'9/{d}/2025' for d in range(1,22)]
base=sub[sub.date.isin(base_dates)]
anom=sub[sub.date==anomaly]

new_fams = set(anom.instance_family.unique()) - set(base.instance_family.unique())
print('new fams:', new_fams)

# check for 9/23..9/29 (the elevated period)
elevated = [f'9/{d}/2025' for d in range(23,30)]
elev = sub[sub.date.isin(elevated)]

# For each new fam: is it present on all elevated days? cost per day
for f in sorted(new_fams):
    e = elev[elev.instance_family==f].groupby('date').unblended_cost.sum()
    a = anom[anom.instance_family==f].unblended_cost.sum()
    print(f, 'anomaly day cost:', round(a,2), '| elevated days:', dict(round(e,1)))

# also check instance_family num_instances on 9/23-29 for the new fams
e2 = elev[elev.instance_family.isin(new_fams)].groupby(['instance_family','date']).num_instances.sum()
print(e2)

import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
sub = df[df.account_id=='tVENWJP'].copy()
anomaly='9/22/2025'
base_dates=[f'9/{d}/2025' for d in range(1,22)]
base=sub[sub.date.isin(base_dates)]
anom=sub[sub.date==anomaly]

# num_instances change per instance_family, including zeros
b=base.groupby('instance_family').num_instances.mean().reindex(base.instance_family.unique(),fill_value=0)
a=anom.groupby('instance_family').num_instances.sum()
allf = set(b.index)|set(a.index)
b=b.reindex(allf,fill_value=0); a=a.reindex(allf,fill_value=0)
chg=(a-b).sort_values(key=abs,ascending=False)
print(chg.head(15))
print('total num_instances change:', chg.sum())

# cost change per instance_family including new ones
bc=base.groupby('instance_family').unblended_cost.mean().reindex(allf,fill_value=0)
ac=anom.groupby('instance_family').unblended_cost.sum().reindex(allf,fill_value=0)
cc=(ac-bc).sort_values(key=abs,ascending=False)
print(cc.head(15))
print('total cost change:', cc.sum())

# check the 0sCXpDQUOa daily series
fam='0sCXpDQUOa'
print(sub[sub.instance_family==fam].groupby('date')[['num_instances','unblended_cost']].sum().tail(12))
